//: SEPARATE tsconfig project, for the same reason apps/web/functions has one: this is Workers-runtime code, not Node. The root tsconfig's include is `apps/*/src/**/*.ts`, which WOULD match apps/usage-worker/src/**, so without excluding it there the Worker would be typechecked with @types/node present and DOM absent — exactly backwards. That combination type-errors on crypto.subtle/Request/Response while silently ACCEPTING process.env and Buffer, which do not exist in the Workers runtime.
//lib: DOM supplies Request/Response/URL/crypto.subtle/TextEncoder. D1Database, KVNamespace and ScheduledController come from a hand-written ambient declaration in src/env.d.ts rather than from @cloudflare/workers-types.
//types: types is EMPTY, and that is load-bearing. Setting types to ["@cloudflare/workers-types"] made `process.env.HOME` and `Buffer.from()` typecheck CLEANLY in this project — measured, not assumed — because that package ships Node compat globals. Neither exists in the deployed runtime, so the guard would have been blind to exactly the mistake it is here to catch. apps/web/functions/tsconfig.json uses types: [] for the same reason and correctly reports TS2591 for `process`.
//run: Checked by `pnpm typecheck:worker`, which `pnpm typecheck` chains — the guard must be wired into the aggregate command or it is a guard that never runs.
//js: allowJs+checkJs and the .js glob exist for ONE file: src/pages-entry.js, which is copied byte-for-byte into the deployed dist/usage as `_worker.js` (Pages advanced mode expects JavaScript, and adding a bundler to this workflow for 40 lines is not worth the dependency). Without the glob it would be the one Workers-runtime file in the repo that nothing typechecks — and it is the file that decides whether the private report is world-readable.
